key_insight: OMOP standardization combined with NLP and PSA-based algorithms improved prostate cancer data completeness and research readiness, rather than directly advancing drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: More complete longitudinal prostate cancer records could support observational research on treatment and recurrence, but clinical benefits were not evaluated.
method: Mapped UTMB Epic EHR data for registry-identified patients from 2010–2021 to OMOP CDM v5.4.
Used NLP to extract PSA values, Gleason scores, and cancer stage from clinical text.
Applied PSA-based algorithms to identify missing treatment information and biochemical recurrence.
evidence_signal: Of 815 analytic cases, 700 (85.9%) were complete and concordant with registry data; NLP improved sparse pathology capture, and PSA trajectories identified 60 biochemical recurrence cases.
watch_item: Single-institution findings and errors found in registry data warrant external validation of extraction and inference algorithms.
paper_title: Developing an OMOP-Standardized Prostate Cancer Database and Improving Data Quality Using NLP and PSA-Based Algorithms
